prompt: Complete ListSerializer so save turns an ArrayList<String> into a byte array via ObjectOutputStream and load restores it via ObjectInputStream (an unchecked cast with @SuppressWarnings is fine).
explanation: ArrayList already implements Serializable, so writeObject serializes the list along with every element in it -- collections of Serializable elements round-trip in one call. Generics are erased at runtime, so readObject can only return Object; the cast to ArrayList<String> is unchecked and @SuppressWarnings("unchecked") acknowledges that the compiler cannot verify the element type. The loaded list is a completely independent copy of the original.
hints: The whole list is one object: out.writeObject(items) serializes it and all its elements.
In load, readObject() returns Object -- cast it to java.util.ArrayList<String>.
Put @SuppressWarnings("unchecked") on the load method to silence the cast warning.
